content.content: {"result":"{\"documentId\": \"f_6feda53b2382c63bf47b25\", \"title\": \"Angel note: how to count the money\", \"name\": \"Angel note: how to count the money\", \"revisionId\": \"a7f6f837df\", \"createdTime\": \"2026-02-12T23:52:18Z\", \"modifiedTime\": \"2026-02-13T00:41:06Z\", \"text\": \"Angel note: how to count the money\\nAngels will ask what each bet cost and what it brought in. This is how we count it so the three of us say the same thing. It replaces the quick plan I left on our board.\\nGo by the bank. SVB\\u2019s Payment Processed notices are the one place I know with a line per payment, and what the banks say is our ground source of truth. Start at the first SVB wires in Sep 2023 and stop at the last run on Feb 2. Anything paid out of Chase isn\\u2019t in here.\\nWhat counts is money that left the company and stayed out. A notice is where you start, not the last word. Take a notice as paid unless one of us has said the money came back. If someone we paid closes out their file with us and tells us what they received, that beats the notices for them. Money we moved between our own accounts isn\\u2019t spending, no bucket for that. Every payee keeps its line, even at zero.\\nIf we paid a contractor some other way, it goes in only if a receipt for it reached your mail, at the amount sent, not the fee.\\nBuckets. Build is the team on Deel plus the studios and freelancers who made the games. Everything on Deel counts as team, don\\u2019t try to split it. Marketing is anything made or bought to get installs (ad networks, agencies, ad creative, playables, trailers): list it under its bet by date like the rest, but keep it out of build cost, I have those numbers. Company is legal, tools, the website, equipment and anything else that wasn\\u2019t for one of the three games: that goes in the Company column. Our own pay and anyone on Gusto aren\\u2019t in here.\\nWhich bet. Go by the Transaction Date on the notice, the whole payment to one bet: Domino Delights up to Jan 8, 2025, ZM from Jan 9, 2025 to Nov 23, 2025, Combo Fighter from Nov 24, 2025. Don\\u2019t try to work out who was on what, that\\u2019s where we\\u2019d start arguing.\\nAnything not paid in dollars stays in its own currency next to the line. Don\\u2019t add it to a dollar total.\\nWhat each game brought in is its lifetime revenue from the warehouse\\u2019s daily revenue table, as recorded. Leave Combo Fighter\\u2019s revenue off for now, on the page, on the deck and when you tell me, until we\\u2019ve checked its first sales.\\nOn the Linear project: move each payee\\u2019s issue to Done once its line is right. If your figure isn\\u2019t what the notices add up to, say why on the issue first.\\n\"}"}

{"documentId": "f_6feda53b2382c63bf47b25", "title": "Angel note: how to count the money", "name": "Angel note: how to count the money", "revisionId": "a7f6f837df", "createdTime": "2026-02-12T23:52:18Z", "modifiedTime": "2026-02-13T00:41:06Z", "text": "Angel note: how to count the money
Angels will ask what each bet cost and what it brought in. This is how we count it so the three of us say the same thing. It replaces the quick plan I left on our board.
Go by the bank. SVB’s Payment Processed notices are the one place I know with a line per payment, and what the banks say is our ground source of truth. Start at the first SVB wires in Sep 2023 and stop at the last run on Feb 2. Anything paid out of Chase isn’t in here.
What counts is money that left the company and stayed out. A notice is where you start, not the last word. Take a notice as paid unless one of us has said the money came back. If someone we paid closes out their file with us and tells us what they received, that beats the notices for them. Money we moved between our own accounts isn’t spending, no bucket for that. Every payee keeps its line, even at zero.
If we paid a contractor some other way, it goes in only if a receipt for it reached your mail, at the amount sent, not the fee.
Buckets. Build is the team on Deel plus the studios and freelancers who made the games. Everything on Deel counts as team, don’t try to split it. Marketing is anything made or bought to get installs (ad networks, agencies, ad creative, playables, trailers): list it under its bet by date like the rest, but keep it out of build cost, I have those numbers. Company is legal, tools, the website, equipment and anything else that wasn’t for one of the three games: that goes in the Company column. Our own pay and anyone on Gusto aren’t in here.
Which bet. Go by the Transaction Date on the notice, the whole payment to one bet: Domino Delights up to Jan 8, 2025, ZM from Jan 9, 2025 to Nov 23, 2025, Combo Fighter from Nov 24, 2025. Don’t try to work out who was on what, that’s where we’d start arguing.
Anything not paid in dollars stays in its own currency next to the line. Don’t add it to a dollar total.
What each game brought in is its lifetime revenue from the warehouse’s daily revenue table, as recorded. Leave Combo Fighter’s revenue off for now, on the page, on the deck and when you tell me, until we’ve checked its first sales.
On the Linear project: move each payee’s issue to Done once its line is right. If your figure isn’t what the notices add up to, say why on the issue first.
"}

cat > /tmp/agg.py <<'EOF'
import json,datetime,collections
recs=json.load(open('/tmp/recs.json'))
def dt(s): return datetime.datetime.strptime(s,'%b %d %Y').date()
def bet(d):
    if d<=datetime.date(2025,1,8): return 'DD'
    if d<=datetime.date(2025,11,23): return 'ZM'
    return 'CF'
refs=collections.Counter(r['ref'] for r in recs)
print('dup refs',[k for k,v in refs.items() if v>1])
tot=collections.defaultdict(float)
for r in recs:
    a,c=r['amt'].split(); a=float(a.replace(',',''))
    if c=='USD': tot[bet(dt(r['tdate']))]+=a
    else: print('nonusd',r)
print(dict(tot))
# by payee
acct=lambda r:r['to'].split('***')[-1]
pp=collections.defaultdict(lambda: collections.defaultdict(float))
for r in recs:
    a,c=r['amt'].split(); a=float(a.replace(',',''))
    pp[acct(r)][bet(dt(r['tdate']))+('' if c=='USD' else c)]+=a
for k,v in sorted(pp.items()): print(k,dict(v))
EOF
python3 /tmp/agg.py

Who is the primary target audience?*
The core audience is teen and adult Barbie fans who already enjoy cozy life sims and light idle games on mobile.
• Roughly 13 to 55, predominantly female.
• Strong overlap with players of fashion, home design, and lifestyle sim titles.
• Comfortable with deeper collection, progression, and event systems, and with free to play economy patterns.
A secondary audience is Barbie loving kids around 8 to 12 who will naturally arrive through the brand, siblings, parents, and discovery in app stores. We are not designing the systems around young children, but the experience is friendly and intuitive enough that they can still have fun within safe boundaries.
The product is a free to play idle life sim aimed at a teen plus audience, with meaningful progression, collection, and profession systems to support long term engagement and monetization. At the same time, themes, visuals, and tone stay within PEGI 3 and ESRB E style expectations so that the game remains positive, aspirational, and safe if younger players join.

*2. Is the game built for teens, young adults, or children?*
The design target is teens and young adults, with adults welcome, and children protected.
• Systems depth, economy, and long term goals are tuned for players 13 plus who are used to free to play games and can engage with more complex progression and collection.
• Content, tone, and themes remain family friendly and brand safe, so if an 8 to 12 year old plays alongside an older sibling or parent, the experience still feels appropriate and positive.
This gives Barbie a mobile product that speaks to the broader fandom while staying fully aligned with Mattel standards.

*3. If needed, how would the concept adapt to PEGI 3?*
Our baseline plan is already aligned with PEGI 3 style requirements. If needed, we can go further and tighten around formal PEGI and ESRB guidance in collaboration with your brand and compliance teams. Concretely:
• No bad language, explicit conflict, or frightening imagery.
• No romantic content that would Push the rating beyond PEGI 3.
• Visuals that emphasize colorful, toy like environments instead of realistic intensity.
• Clear UI and parental friendly settings for things like purchases and online features.
We would work directly with the Mattel team and your publishing partner to review early assets, copy, and features, and treat ratings compliance as a core gate at each milestone, not a late stage patch.

Instead, the configuration for IAP and the distinction between sandbox and production environments are handled through your project settings and the way you handle IAP within your game’s code.

When you are preparing your application for IAP in Unity, it’s important to integrate your game with Apple’s StoreKit API through a native code plugin. This setup includes defining the types of products you’ll be selling (like content, functionality, services, or subscriptions) and using AssetBundles for downloadable content if necessary. This process is described in detail in Unity’s documentation on preparing your application for In-App Purchases.

The process of setting up Unity IAP for the Apple App Store involves writing a game that implements Unity IAP, keeping track of your product identifiers for use in iTunes Connect, registering your application with an explicit App ID (since wildcard App IDs cannot be used for IAP), and setting up your in-app purchases in iTunes Connect.

For testing IAPs, you’ll need to create Sandbox Testers in iTunes Connect. When testing on a device, make sure to sign out of any existing Apple IDs and only sign in with the Sandbox Tester account when prompted by the app. This ensures that any subsequent purchases are routed through the Apple Sandbox instead of the Production Store. The in-game purchase dialog will display a notification indicating that the purchase is being performed in the Sandbox Environment.

The Unity documentation on configuring for Apple App Store and Mac App Store, as well as Apple’s documentation on testing in-app purchases with sandbox, provide comprehensive guides on these processes.

It’s important to note that the environment (sandbox or production) your app connects to for IAP is determined by the Apple ID used on the device during testing (a sandbox tester Apple ID for sandbox testing) and not by a specific file in your Unity project.

For more detailed information, you can refer to Unity’s documentation on [Preparing your application for In-App Purchases](<https://docs.unity3d.com/2021.3/Documentation/Manual/iphone-Downloadable-Content.html>) and [Configuring for Apple App Store and Mac App Store](<https://docs.unity3d.com/2021.2/Documentation/Manual/UnityIAPAppleConfiguration.html>), as well as Apple’s [Testing in-app purchases with sandbox](<https://developer.Apple.com/documentation/storekit/in-app_purchase/testing_in-app_purchases_with_sandbox>) documentation.", "channel": "C04UTBZL6AX", "user": "EMPLOYEE_0038_SLACK_ID", "channel_info": {"id": "C04UTBZL6AX", "name": "founders", "is_private": true, "is_im": false, "is_mpim": false}, "user_profile": {"id": "EMPLOYEE_0038_SLACK_ID", "name": "Leonard Hayes", "real_name": "Leonard Hayes", "display_name": "Leonard Hayes", "email": "leonard.hayes@harmonygames.co"}, "time": "2024-01-14T21:08:21Z", "permalink": "https://harmonygamesgroup.slack.com/archives/C04UTBZL6AX/p1705266501850339"}, {"ts": "1705265957.516239", "type": "message", "text": "the account was set with media purchases off by default", "channel": "C04UTBZL6AX", "user": "EMPLOYEE_0038_SLACK_ID", "channel_info": {"id": "C04UTBZL6AX", "name": "founders", "is_private": true, "is_im": false, "is_mpim": false}, "user_profile": {"id": "EMPLOYEE_0038_SLACK_ID", "name": "Leonard Hayes", "real_name": "Leonard Hayes", "display_name": "Leonard Hayes", "email": "leonard.hayes@harmonygames.co"}, "time": "2024-01-14T20:59:17Z", "permalink": "https://harmonygamesgroup.slack.com/archives/C04UTBZL6AX/p1705265957516239"}, {"ts": "1705265301.921329", "type": "message", "text": "The error message “iTunes account creation not allowed. Here are some common causes and troubleshooting steps you might consider:

1. **Product Identifier Mismatch**: Ensure that the product identifiers in your app’s code match exactly with those set up in App Store Connect. Even a minor discrepancy (like a typo) can cause products to not be fetched correctly.

2. **Products Not Configured Correctly in App Store Connect**: Double-check that your IAP products are correctly configured in App Store Connect. They should be in the right status (like ‘Ready to Submit’ or ‘Approved’) and associated with the correct app.

3. **Issue with the Sandbox Tester Account**: Make sure the sandbox tester account is properly set up and active. If There’s an issue with the account (like not being verified), it could prevent access to IAPs.

4. **Problems with StoreKit Implementation**: Review your StoreKit implementation in your app’s code. It’s possible There might be an issue in the way you are requesting products or initializing the payment queue.

5. **Network Issues**: Sometimes, network issues can prevent your app from communicating with Apple’s servers to fetch the IAP products. Make sure you have a stable internet connection.

6. **App’s Bundle ID Mismatch**: The bundle ID in your app’s code must match the bundle ID you used to set up the app in App Store Connect. A mismatch here can lead to issues with fetching IAPs.

7. **Region and Locale Settings**: Check if the region and locale settings of your test device match those supported by your IAPs. Some IAPs may be restricted to certain regions.

8. **App Not Signed in with Sandbox Tester Account**: Ensure that you’re signed into the App Store with the sandbox tester account on your testing device. Remember to sign out of your regular Apple ID first.

9. **Check for Console Logs or Error Messages**: Sometimes, the Xcode console or device logs can provide more detailed error messages that can help diagnose the issue.

10. **Update Your Testing Device and Tools**: Make sure that your testing device and development tools (like Xcode) are updated to the latest version, as older versions might have compatibility issues.

If none of these steps resolve the issue, it might be helpful to consult Apple’s Developer Forums or reach out to Apple Developer Support for further assistance. The sandbox environment allows you to test IAPs without making actual purchases. Here’s a general overview of the process:

1. **Create Sandbox Tester Accounts**: In your App Store Connect account, create sandbox tester accounts. These accounts are used to simulate the purchase process in your app.

2. **Configure Your App for IAP**: Make sure your app is properly configured to handle IAPs. This includes setting up the IAP items in App Store Connect, and implementing the code in your app to handle the purchase process.

3. **Implement IAP Code**: In your app, use the StoreKit framework to implement IAP functionality. This includes fetching available IAPs, presenting them to the user, and handling the purchase flow.

4. **Testing in Sandbox Environment**: Install the app on a test device. Sign out of your regular Apple ID on the device, and then sign in with a sandbox tester account. It’s important not to use your regular Apple ID, as sandbox tester accounts are separate.

5. **Simulate Purchases**: Within the app, attempt to purchase IAPs. The purchase dialogs will indicate that you are in the sandbox environment. Follow the prompts to complete the purchase.

6. **Handle Transactions**: Ensure that your app correctly handles successful and failed transactions. In the sandbox environment, you can test different scenarios like successful purchases, cancellations, and failed transactions.

7. **Verify Receipts**: In the sandbox environment, your app can verify receipts with Apple’s sandbox server. This is crucial for validating that the purchase was successful and legitimate.

8. **Test Different Scenarios**: Test different IAP scenarios, including consumable and non-consumable purchases, auto-renewable subscriptions, and free trials.

9. **Check for Common Issues**: If you encounter errors, check for common issues like incorrect product identifiers, issues with the sandbox tester account, or issues with the network connection.

10. **Consult Documentation**: Refer to Apple’s official documentation for detailed guidance on each step, including specific code implementations and troubleshooting tips.

Remember, the sandbox environment is designed to mimic the live App Store environment, but it’s specifically for testing purposes. Transactions made in the sandbox environment are not real transactions and won’t be charged.

For detailed instructions and guidelines, you should consult the [In-App Purchase Programming Guide](<https://developer.Apple.com/in-app-purchase/>) and [testflight documentation](<https://developer.Apple.com/testflight/>). progression. Here\\u2019s a breakdown of key events and data points to track:\\n\\n### 1. **Player Actions**\\n   - **Tile Drop Events**: Capture each time a player drops a tile, including the selected drop point (specific column) and the number of remaining tiles.\\n   - **Drop Point Choices**: Track which of the available columns (e.g., 1 to 9, depending on board configuration) players select for each tile drop.\\n   - **Tile Bank**: Monitor the player\\u2019s balance of Plinko tiles and how many are dropped per session. Also track the max cap of tiles (default 50) and whether players purchase extra tiles.\\n   - **Reset Prize Reel**: Capture when players pay currency to reset the prize reel or extend the reset timer for any column.\\n\\n### 2. **Game Events**\\n   - **Tile Landing**: Record where each tile lands, specifying the prize column (e.g., position 1, 2, 3, or 4). This should be logged alongside the chosen drop point.\\n   - **Prize Reel Spin**: Track the outcome of each prize reel spin, including the tier of the prize and whether a jackpot was hit (99% standard, 1% jackpot).\\n   - **Prize Tier Progression**: Monitor the progression of prizes in each column, logging when a tile landing increases the prize tier. Include resets and reel extensions.\\n   - **Jackpot Occurrence**: Capture when jackpot prizes are awarded, including visual effects (e.g., aura, flame, glow) triggered by this event.\\n\\n### 3. **Probability and Distribution**\\n   - **Probability Mapping**: Track the probability distribution of tile landings across the prize columns. This will allow you to assess if the board design (e.g., number of columns and rows) is functioning as intended, with more tiles landing in outer columns than the center.\\n   - **Probability vs. Reward**: Track how often tiles land in high-reward (middle) vs low-reward (outer) columns and compare it to the expected probability distribution for optimization purposes.\\n\\n### 4. **Resource Tracking**\\n   - **Prize Collection**: Capture the types and quantities of prizes players win from each prize column, including whether they claim a standard or jackpot reward.\\n   - **Currency Spent**: Monitor how much in-game currency is spent to reset prize reels or extend the prize reset timer.\\n   - **Player Currency Balance**: Track changes in the player\\u2019s currency balance after every reset or reel extension.\\n\\n### 5. **Performance Metrics**\\n   - **Game Time**: Track the duration of each session, including time spent in the Plinko mini-game and how often players return to it.\\n   - **Session Frequency**: Monitor how frequently players engage with the Plinko mini-game over time (e.g., daily or weekly engagement).\\n   - **Tile Drop Frequency**: Record how quickly players drop tiles, whether they drop multiple tiles in quick succession or spread them out over time.\\n\\n### 6. **Player Progression**\\n   - **Prize Reel Tiers**: Capture the current tier for each prize column and track how often players reach higher tiers (e.g., Tier 5 or above).\\n   - **Plinko Tile Acquisition**: Track how players acquire Plinko tiles, whether from leftover tiles in the main game, as rewards, or through purchases.\\n\\n### 7. **user Experience Metrics**\\n   - **Drop Point Popularity**: Measure how frequently players choose each drop point at the top of the board. This can help determine whether players aim for specific columns or distribute their drops randomly.\\n   - **Column-Specific engagement**: Track which prize columns see the most tile landings and prize wins, and whether players concentrate tiles in specific columns to maximize rewards.\\n   - **Frustration Indicators**: Monitor patterns that might indicate player frustration, such as exiting the game after dropping tiles in low-reward slots or resetting the prize reels frequently without achieving desired outcomes.\\n\\n### 8. **Retention & Monetization**\\n   - **Player Retention**: Track how often players return to the Plinko mini-game and whether they return after claiming high-tier rewards.\\n   - **In-App Purchases**: Log the purchase of any items related to Plinko, such as extra tiles or currency to reset prize reels.\\n   - **Prize Impact on Retention**: Analyze whether reaching higher prize tiers or winning jackpot prizes increases player retention.\\n\\nBy tracking these metrics, you can gain valuable insights into how players interact with the Plinko mini-game, how the probability distribution affects rewards, and how players engage with the prize reel mechanics. This should be logged alongside the chosen drop point.\\n   - **Prize Reel Spin**: Track the outcome of each prize reel spin, including the tier of the prize and whether a jackpot was hit (99% standard, 1% jackpot).\\n   - **Prize Tier Progression**: Monitor the progression of prizes in each column, logging when a tile landing increases the prize tier. ### 1. **Player Actions**
   - **Tile Drop Events**: Capture each time a player drops a tile, including the selected drop point (specific column) and the number of remaining tiles.
   - **Drop Point Choices**: Track which of the available columns (e.g., 1 to 9, depending on board configuration) players select for each tile drop.
   - **Tile Bank**: Monitor the player’s balance of Plinko tiles and how many are dropped per session. Also track the max cap of tiles (default 50) and whether players purchase extra tiles.
   - **Reset Prize Reel**: Capture when players pay currency to reset the prize reel or extend the reset timer for any column.

### 2. **Game Events**
   - **Tile Landing**: Record where each tile lands, specifying the prize column (e.g., position 1, 2, 3, or 4). This should be logged alongside the chosen drop point.
   - **Prize Reel Spin**: Track the outcome of each prize reel spin, including the tier of the prize and whether a jackpot was hit (99% standard, 1% jackpot).
   - **Prize Tier Progression**: Monitor the progression of prizes in each column, logging when a tile landing increases the prize tier. Include resets and reel extensions.
   - **Jackpot Occurrence**: Capture when jackpot prizes are awarded, including visual effects (e.g., aura, flame, glow) triggered by this event.

### 3. **Probability and Distribution**
   - **Probability Mapping**: Track the probability distribution of tile landings across the prize columns. This will allow you to assess if the board design (e.g., number of columns and rows) is functioning as intended, with more tiles landing in outer columns than the center.
   - **Probability vs. Reward**: Track how often tiles land in high-reward (middle) vs low-reward (outer) columns and compare it to the expected probability distribution for optimization purposes.

### 4. **Resource Tracking**
   - **Prize Collection**: Capture the types and quantities of prizes players win from each prize column, including whether they claim a standard or jackpot reward.
   - **Currency Spent**: Monitor how much in-game currency is spent to reset prize reels or extend the prize reset timer.
   - **Player Currency Balance**: Track changes in the player’s currency balance after every reset or reel extension.

### 5. **Performance Metrics**
   - **Game Time**: Track the duration of each session, including time spent in the Plinko mini-game and how often players return to it.
   - **Session Frequency**: Monitor how frequently players engage with the Plinko mini-game over time (e.g., daily or weekly engagement).
   - **Tile Drop Frequency**: Record how quickly players drop tiles, whether they drop multiple tiles in quick succession or spread them out over time.

### 6. **Player Progression**
   - **Prize Reel Tiers**: Capture the current tier for each prize column and track how often players reach higher tiers (e.g., Tier 5 or above).
   - **Plinko Tile Acquisition**: Track how players acquire Plinko tiles, whether from leftover tiles in the main game, as rewards, or through purchases.

### 7. **user Experience Metrics**
   - **Drop Point Popularity**: Measure how frequently players choose each drop point at the top of the board. This can help determine whether players aim for specific columns or distribute their drops randomly.
   - **Column-Specific engagement**: Track which prize columns see the most tile landings and prize wins, and whether players concentrate tiles in specific columns to maximize rewards.
   - **Frustration Indicators**: Monitor patterns that might indicate player frustration, such as exiting the game after dropping tiles in low-reward slots or resetting the prize reels frequently without achieving desired outcomes.

### 8. **Retention & Monetization**
   - **Player Retention**: Track how often players return to the Plinko mini-game and whether they return after claiming high-tier rewards.
   - **In-App Purchases**: Log the purchase of any items related to Plinko, such as extra tiles or currency to reset prize reels.
   - **Prize Impact on Retention**: Analyze whether reaching higher prize tiers or winning jackpot prizes increases player retention.

### 4. **Performance Metrics**

   - **Session Frequency**: Track how often players return to the mini-game and how long they spend per session.
   - **Success Rates**: Measure the percentage of tiles that fall into the bottom pit versus those lost in the side pits.
   - **Bomb Explosions**: Track the number of bomb tile explosions and their effects on surrounding tiles.

   - **Hero Level Integration**: Track how hero levels from the main game affect the mini-game (e.g., power-up potency, tile conversion chances).
   - **Salvager Engine Events**: Once integrated, track how main game events influence tile and object appearances in the Tile Dozer mini-game.

   - **Tile Drop Frequency**: Track how frequently players drop tiles (related to regeneration rates and inventory limits).

RAW_GAME_EVENTS and STG_EVENTS_ENRICHED retain a 1:8 session sample, and PROGRESSION_EVENTS, SESSION_LEVEL_EVENTS and AD_IMPRESSION_EVENTS a 1:16 sample, so a recount from those tables will not match these totals.\", \"row_count\": 1682, \"created_at\": \"2023-10-28T00:00:00Z\", \"database\": \"ANALYTICS\", \"schema\": \"GAME_EVENTS\", \"fully_qualified_name\": \"ANALYTICS.GAME_EVENTS.DAILY_ACTIVE_USERS\"}, {\"id\": \"ANALYTICS.GAME_EVENTS.DAILY_METRICS_AGG\", \"schema_id\": \"ANALYTICS.GAME_EVENTS\", \"name\": \"DAILY_METRICS_AGG\", \"table_type\": \"BASE TABLE\", \"comment\": \"Daily metrics mart derived from the DAU and revenue tables. Aggregated upstream of the retained event tables. RAW_GAME_EVENTS and STG_EVENTS_ENRICHED retain a 1:8 session sample, and PROGRESSION_EVENTS, SESSION_LEVEL_EVENTS and AD_IMPRESSION_EVENTS a 1:16 sample, so a recount from those tables will not match these totals.\", \"row_count\": 5497, \"created_at\": \"2023-10-28T00:00:00Z\", \"database\": \"ANALYTICS\", \"schema\": \"GAME_EVENTS\", \"fully_qualified_name\": \"ANALYTICS.GAME_EVENTS.LEVEL_PERFORMANCE\"}, {\"id\": \"ANALYTICS.GAME_EVENTS.PLAYER_DAILY_PROGRESS\", \"schema_id\": \"ANALYTICS.GAME_EVENTS\", \"name\": \"PLAYER_DAILY_PROGRESS\", \"table_type\": \"BASE TABLE\", \"comment\": \"Per-player daily snapshot: level reached, sessions, coins, boosters, levels attempted/completed, purchase flag. coins_earned is what play paid out; coins bought from the store arrive as iap_grant rows in RESOURCE_FLOW_EVENTS and are not counted here. coins_spent and boosters_used count purchases at each game's shipped booster prices, so a player-day with no affordable purchase reads zero, and boosters_used is zero throughout for Combo Fighter, which ships none. made_purchase is reconciled against IAP_TRANSACTIONS at the game-date grain. LEVEL_PERFORMANCE is aggregated from the full upstream event stream before sampling, not from this table, so a recount here will not reproduce it.\", \"row_count\": 176206, \"created_at\": \"2023-11-02T00:00:00Z\", \"database\": \"ANALYTICS\", \"schema\": \"GAME_EVENTS\", \"fully_qualified_name\": \"ANALYTICS.GAME_EVENTS.SESSION_LEVEL_EVENTS\"}, {\"id\": \"ANALYTICS.GAME_EVENTS.USER_COHORT_RETENTION\", \"schema_id\": \"ANALYTICS.GAME_EVENTS\", \"name\": \"USER_COHORT_RETENTION\", \"table_type\": \"BASE TABLE\", \"comment\": \"Weekly install cohorts with Day 1 through Day 60 retention, 333 cohort rows. Done. Here's the page: https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/13xBbqMqgVAFTHVbfPJI7Xd3erEL03_WG3tkYQyr0moQ/edit (it's in my Drive and shared with you and Blake). It uses your Angel note working layout. All 22 Payee history issues are now Done, with a comment on each one where my figure is different from the notices.

**Cost to build** (team on Deel plus the studios and freelancers, split by Transaction Date):
• Domino Delights: **$951,818**
• ZM: **$544,433**
• Combo Fighter: **$72,686**

**Brought in** (lifetime, warehouse REVENUE_DAILY, as recorded):
• Domino Delights: **$12,331**
• ZM: **$12** ($11.99)
• Combo Fighter: left off until we've checked its first sales

**Changes on the draft deck**
• Cost slide: change $985K / $609K / $74K to **$952K / $544K / $73K**
• Brought-in slide: change "to fill in" to **Domino Delights $12.3K, ZM $12**. Leave Combo Fighter off.

**Why it's lower than your quick pass** (yours was every USD notice by date):
• Moved out of build cost: marketing ($16.4K DD, $56.5K ZM, $1K CF: Node Media, Adjoe, AppLovin, PlayableX, the Telegram UA contract) and company costs ($49.6K: Singular, TYZ, trademarks, the website, the 4X proposal)
• Leapblock closed our file yesterday with 407,944 received over 30 wires. The notices only show 29, because the Sep 13 2023 wire of 33,290 never got a Processed notice. I used their figure, which adds $33.3K to DD
• Taken out: the Apr 2024 MotMot wire to ***8605 that came back ($4,032), the $4,000 to JPMorgan ***3203 (Blake confirmed it went to our own Chase account), and Oleg's $125 (it came back, and no Payoneer receipt for the resend ever reached my mail)
• Martin's laptop stays in leva (BGN 1,999) on the Company line and isn't in any dollar total

I've built the one-page sheet, closed out the Payee history project and replied to Leonard in #winddown. The build costs come to $951,818 for Domino Delights, $544,433 for ZM and $72,686 for Combo Fighter. Every dollar on the SVB notices is either in a column or explained in a note.

**The sheet:** [Angel note: what each bet cost and brought in](https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/13xBbqMqgVAFTHVbfPJI7Xd3erEL03_WG3tkYQyr0moQ/edit). It's in your Drive, shared with Leonard and Blake as editors, and uses the same layout as Leonard's working sheet. All 22 payees have a line, including the ones at zero.

**What each bet cost and brought in:**

| | Cost to build | Brought in (lifetime) |
|---|---|---|
| Domino Delights | $951,818 | $12,331 |
| ZM | $544,433 | $12 |
| Combo Fighter | $72,686 | left off, as Leonard asked |

Revenue comes from the warehouse's daily revenue table.

**Changes on the draft deck:**
- **Cost slide:** $985K / $609K / $74K becomes $952K / $544K / $73K.
- **Brought-in slide:** "to fill in" becomes Domino Delights $12.3K and ZM $12, with Combo Fighter left off. Leonard said he'll make the edits himself.

**Where it differs from Leonard's quick numbers** (his were every dollar notice, split by date):
- **Marketing out of build cost:** $73.9K for Node Media, Adjoe, AppLovin, PlayableX and the Telegram ad contractor. It's still listed under each bet by date.
- **Company costs in their own column:** $49.6K for Singular, the lawyers, trademarks, the website and the 4X proposal.
- **Leapblock:** they closed our file yesterday and confirmed $407,944 received over 30 wires. Only 29 have a "Processed" notice; the first one, $33,290 on Sep 13, 2023, never got one. Leonard's rule is that a payee's own close-out beats the notices, so I used their figure, which adds $33,290 to Domino Delights.
- **Wires that came back, taken out:**
  - The April 2024 MotMot wire to the wrong account ($4,032). Leonard confirmed it in #admin_foundersonly; it was re-sent and is counted once.
  - Oleg's $125. The re-send went through Payoneer, but the only Payoneer emails in your inbox are payment requests from him, not a receipt.
- **Transfer, taken out:** the $4,000 to "JPMorgan" in Aug 2024 was a move to our own Chase account, per Blake's Feb 13 email.
- **Martin's laptop** stays in Bulgarian leva (1,999) on the Company line and isn't in any dollar total.

**Linear:** before closing them I commented on the four payees where my figure doesn't match the notices: Leapblock, MotMot, the Chase transfer and Oleg. Then I moved all 22 issues to Done.

Sources: Slack (#winddown, #leapblock, #admin_foundersonly), Gmail (SVB notices, Blake's Chase email, Node Media invoices, Payoneer requests), Linear Payee history comments, Snowflake revenue table, Leonard's counting doc, working sheet and draft deck.
